title: Santuvario, a natural wine producer in Alto Piemonte, Italy
summary: Santuvario is a small natural wine producer based in the town of Borgomanero in Alto Piemonte, at the foot of
content:
Santuvario is a small natural wine producer based in the town of Borgomanero in Alto Piemonte, at the foot of the alps. The wine region is called Boca, and has been growing smaller. At one stage there were 1000 hectares here; now there are just 10.

The people behind Santuvario are Ivano Barbaglia and Paola Fornara, who began making these wines in 2012. Altitude here is between 400 and 500 m, and they farm old vines including Nebbiolo, Vespolina, Uva Rara and Croatina.

One interesting feature about the vineyards is a distinctive old training system called Maggiorina. I tasted these wines at the VinNatur event in Paris, November 2025.

Santuvario Gino Bianco 2022 Piemonte, Italy
12.5% alcohol. This is made from the Erbaluce grape variety, and it spends one month on skins. Honey, apple and spice on the nose. The palate is grainy with nice grip. Citrus, spice, and lovely depth and flavour. 93/100

Santuvario Lazio 2022 Piemonte, Italy
This is a blend of 80% Nebbiolo with 20% Vespolina, aged for three years in 500 and 1700 litre oak. Juicy, vivid and bright with nice energy. Sour cherry and raspberry fruit with some redcurrant brightness. There’s also some spicy structure. Refined and delicious with a savoury twist and also some structure as well as the fruit. 94/100

Santuvario Red Blend 2020 Piemonte, Italy
This is a blend of Croatina, Nebbiolo, Vespolino and Uvarara aged in 1700 litre oak. Juicy and energetic with raspberries and cherries, as well as some sweet acidity. Spicy and grippy with nice density. Alive, with nice brightness, as well as good depth and structure. 92/100

Santuvario Lavigna 2022 Piemonte, Italy
This is 100% Croatina aged in 500 litre oak. Dense and focused with sweet fruit, as well as nice grip. There’s a floral quality. Grippy and grainy and spicy with a lovely texture, bounded by sweet acidity. 93/100

UK agent: https://www.senlondon.com/

title: Highlights: Tio Pepe Fino Sherry En Rama NV (2026 release)
summary: For me, the en rama movement in Sherry and Manzanilla has been an exciting shift for the region. Big sherry
content:
For me, the en rama movement in Sherry and Manzanilla has been an exciting shift for the region. Big sherry was boring, and then suddenly big Sherry realized they could make very interesting wines simply by not doing the big sherry thing, and bottling without denuding the wines by filtration and clarification. There’s more to the story, told here. But the result is wines like this, from Gonzalez Byass. Big Sherry doing things well.

Tio Pepe Fino En Rama NV Spain (2026 release)
15% alcohol. Yellow/gold in colour, this is bold and incisive, with amazing complexity. We have some spicy, raisiny richness, a feeling of slight sweetness, savoury nuttiness and then some vivid, tangy, crystalline citrus character. This is a wine that’s very rich but also very fresh, with beautiful layered complexity, finishing delightfully salty. It’s just so gastronomic, and utterly delicious. I can’t remember enjoying this wine as much before, even though I’ve rated it highly. It’s one of the great bargains of the fine wine world. 95/100 (£22 The Wine Society, Tanners, Amps, Cork & Cask, Saxtys)

title: Otrepò Pavese Classese: tasting through a large range of these impressive Pinot Noir-based sparkling wines from northwest Italy
summary: I’ve been to a lot of wine regions around the world, but I’m yet to visit the scenic Oltrepò Pavese
content:
I’ve been to a lot of wine regions around the world, but I’m yet to visit the scenic Oltrepò Pavese region in the northwest of Italy. It’s part of Lombardy, and buts up against the Apennine mountains, hence there are hills and some altitude. It’s neighboured by Piemonte, Liguria and Emilia Romagna.

Still wines are made here, but the focus of this tasting was Classese, traditional method sparkling wines from Pinot Noir. The tasting was organized for the Consorzio by Nelson Pari and Federico Moccia.

Currently the region produces fewer than 1 million bottles, compared with Franciacorta which makes 20 million of traditional method sparkling. But this has been growing quite fast, with a production of 400 000 bottles two years ago, then 600 000 a year ago, currently 800 000 and then probably 1 million next year.  

Riccardo Binda, who is the director of the Consorzio, says that it’s not unrealistic to expect a future production level of 5 million bottles, depending on the market. Currently, the largest producer in the region makes 150 000 bottles.

The rules for Otrepò Pavese Classese are that the wine must be from Pinot Noir and spend at least two years on the lees. This is the only region with exclusively Pinot Noir traditional method sparkling in Italy.

There are four towns in the region at the end of each valley, and 40 villages. Wine is made from vineyards at altitudes ranging from 200-600 m. Of the 150 wine producers in the region, 45 make sparkling. Just two producers in the region specialize solely in sparkling.

Classese is on par with the best Blancs de Noirs in the world, says Riccardo. Traditional method sparkling has been made here since 1865. The reason we haven’t heard more about these wines is that the best grapes and wines have typically ended up in other regions, such as Piemonte. ‘What we are trying to do now is give it the place that it deserves in the world of sparkling,’ he says. ‘It is the only region that focuses just on sparkling Pinot Noir.’

We began with a blind tasting of six bottles. We weren’t told anything about what they were: I assumed they were all Oltrepò Pavese, but it turned out to be a mix of Oltrepò and Pinot Noir-based Champagnes, and the Champagnes were all in magnum. These are my notes as written.

Champagne Bollinger PN AYC21 France
12.5% alcohol. Fresh and bright with some toasty richness. Lovely depth to this, with marzipan, honey, nuts and spice supplying richness. And cherry and lime with a hint of salt on the finish. Juicy with lovely energy. 95/100

Monsupello Blanc de Noirs Clasese NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
13% alcohol. Lovely depth here with nice zesty lime, some toasty notes and some subtle nuttiness. Ripe with a slight herby edge to the cherry and apple fruit. Very stylish. 93/100

Ballabio Farfalla Cave Privée Vecchie Vigne 2018 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Expansive with lovely cherry and pear fruit as well as a hint of apple. Nice lemony notes. Linear and precise with nice energy and good focus to the fruit. Stylish with nice presence and a savoury twist. Good balance. 92/100

Champagne Philipponnat Blanc de Noirs Extra Brut 2019 France
12.50% alcohol. Zesty and vivid with intense citrus fruit drive as well as some cherry notes. Lively with a salty lick. Real precision and focus showing lovely cherry fruit. 93/100

Champagne Fleury BdN Extra Brut NV France
12.50% alcohol. Juicy and bright with nice presence and some orange peel and lemon zest notes, as well as some cherry. Nice texture and presence. 93/100

Calatroni Poggio dei Duca 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
48 months on lees. Toast and lemon on the nose. Nice appley richness, with lemon and lime fruit. Has real depth of fruit. Such depth here: rich but well balanced. 94/100

Then it was time to taste through a broad selection of Classese wines.

Bruno Verdi Vergomberra Dosage Zero 2012 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy       
12.5% alcohol. This winery started making traditional method sparkling in 1985, which was right at the beginning for the region. Taut and focused with lovely cherry and almond notes, showing nice depth with a hint of melon. Lime, pit and cherry notes. This is linear with nice depth and a salty finish. 93/100

Bosco Longhino Casto 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12% alcohol. Juicy and bright with nice freshness. Lovely pure lemon and green apple fruit, with nice presence. There’s a hint of pithiness, too. Stylish. 90/100

Brandolini I Ger 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
11.5% alcohol. Juicy and energetic with nice pear and peach fruit, showing some saline notes and nice energy. Lemony and dense, and quite expressive with a nice acid line. Good weight and focus, with some glace cherry notes. 93/100

Bruno Verdi Vergomberra Dosage Zero 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Linear with bice juiciness, and pear and white peach fruit, with some spicy depth. Toast, cherry and peach richness, but it’s also juicy and energetic, with a nice bitter twist on the finish. 92/100

Ca’del Gè Brut 2018 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Crystalline citrus with some pear and peach richness. Toasty and refined with real finesse. 92/100

Ca’Tessitori LB9 Dossagio Zero NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Juicy and lemony with with nice cherry and citrus fruit. Supple with nice energy and good acidity. Pithy and bright. 91/100

Castello di Cigognola Cuvée dell’Angelo 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Supple, bright and pure with nice acidity. Fresh cherry notes with good focus and a touch of apple and pear. 91/100

Cavallotti Riserva del Fondatore Classese 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12% alcohol. Juicy, pithy and bright with nice pure cherry and citrus fruit. Zesty and alert with a nice salty twist. 90/100

Conte Vistarino Pinot Nero Extra Brut 1865 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Supple and bright with nice energy. Has subtle toast and spice wiyh lovely brightness, and a nice saline, herby twist. 93/100

Cordero Brut Millesimato 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Grapey and fresh with nice aromatics. Juicy and grapey with nice brightness. Fruity with a hint of almond. Tart finish. 90/100

Corte Fabbri Elena 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Lively and aromatic with bright citrus fruit. Juicy and herby, and quite expressive. 90/100

Fiamberti Caristoro Extra Brut NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Fine toast, spice and cherries with nice precision. Juicy and bright with some herbal detail. Very expressive with a saline twist. Pure. 93/100

Finigeto 2005 Pas Dosé 2022 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Juicy, bright, fresh and vivid with nice energy. Lemony with a salty finish. Bright, juicy and alert. 91/100

Fradé Dasdot Pas Dosé 2019 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Warm and herbal with nice sweet pear and cherry fruit, as well as some toasty depth. Expressive. 88/100

Frecciarossa Pinot Nero Extra Brut 2022 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Toast, pear and spice as well as white peach and cherry fruit. Nice richness here. Pretty and expressive with sweet fruit and lovely balance. 92/100

Giorgi 1870 T.O.P. Zero Classese NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Linear and bright with nice freshness. Pithy with a herby edge to the angular citrus and cherry fruit. 89/100

Il Feudo Nico Maria Antonietta Classese 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12% alcohol. Juicy and zesty with nice bright herb-scented cherry fruit. Juicy and lively with a touch of sweetness. Zippy and delicious. 90/100

Isimbarda Dosaggio Zero NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Fresh, bright and pithy with lemon and cherry fruit as well as some nice pear richness. Juicy and linear. Pure. 90/100

Rossetti & Scrivani Bland de Noir NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
Juicy and bright with some pear and cherry fruit, as well as a hint of toast. Nice weight with lovely depth. 92/100

La Genisia Centodieci Nature 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Nice herby cherry and pear fruit with appealing orange peel and mandarin notes. There’s a nice savoury twist here with good energy. Supple and delicious. 90/100

La Piotta Riva dei Ghiaioni Pas Dosé 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Juicy and bright with nice citrus, pear and apple fruit. Lovely concentration. Juicy with nice finesse, and a slight bitter cherry note on the finish. 89/100

La Travaglina Martinburgo Classese 2018 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Fresh, toasty and fine with some pithy notes as well as nice pear and peach fruit, with a hint of apple. Lovely focus and freshness here, with a nice hint of pithiness. 92/100

Le Fiole Isabèl Brut 2022 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy  
12.5% alcohol. Nice subtle toast and pear, as well as bright citrus. There’s a touch of cherry, too. This shows nice depth and intensity. 92/100

Lozza Blanc de Noir Pinot Noir Dossagio Zero 2018 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Supple with nice cherry fruit and some almond hints. Juicy and bright with good weight. Supple, juicy and quite salty. 89/100

Manuelina 137 Classese Brut 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Compact with nice citrus and pear fruit as well as some orange peel. Zesty and bold with cherry and a lick of salinity. Nice brightness and purity. 92/100

Marchesi di Montalto Costagrossa Extra Brut 42 Mesi 2016 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Complex and bright, and pithy. Shows nice cherry and pear fruit with a hint of bitterness. Nice precision here with some toast and honey, showing lovely weight. 92/100

Mazzolino Blanc de Noir 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.50% alcohol. Nicely focused with bright cherry and lemon fruit. Pure and linear with lovely focus. Bright. 91/100

Montelio 17 Fiorile 1803 Extra Brut Classese 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% Juicy, bright and zippy with nice linear citrus fruit. Pure and crisp with a touch of cherry and an appealing salty twist. Very stylish. 93/100

Oltrenero Pinot Nero Brut Nature 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.6% alcohol. Juicy and bright with nice freshness and a slight salty twist, with nice pithy hints. Shows real precision: very expressive. 92/100

Picchi Brut Nature Classese 2022 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
13% alcohol. Linear and focused with nice brisk cherry and lemon fruit. Zippy with good acidity and a pleasant bitter twist on the finish. Stylish. 90/100

Prime Alture Io Per Te Classese 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Sweet fruit with nice cherry and pear, with some brightness. Slight salty twist. Some herbs, with lovely focus, finishing sweet. 89/100

Quaquarini Classese Pinot Nero Brut 2019 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Lively and focused, with pure citrus fruit. Nice cherry notes and some toast and pear too. This combines richness and freshness to good effect. 91/100

Scuropasso Roccapietra Zero Classese 2020 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
13% alcohol. 60 months on lees, from this sparkling-only estate. Juicy and bright with taut cherry and pear fruit, showing nice precision. Lime and sour cherry, with some pithy hints. 91/100

Cantina Taia Blanc de Noir Classese 2022 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Pithy and alert with a touch of reduction. There’s a herby edge to the pithy citrus and cherry fruit. Creamy notes, too. 88/100

Torre Degli Alberi Pas Dosé 2021 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Juicy and lemony with detail. Liquorice and herbs complement the appealing lemony fruit. Saline with nice depth. 93/100

Travaglino Vincenzo Comi Reserva del Fondatore 2017 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Fine, toasty and refined with nice weight to the sweet pear and white peach fruit, with a touch of cherry fruit and a hint of sweetness. 91/100

Vanzini Aiace Brut NV Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Notes of pear and peach, with zesty citrus and a touch of sour cherry. 84/100

La Versa Principio Testarossa 2008 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Open apple and pear with a touch of marmalade. Linear and saline with hints of toast, peach and pear, with real precision. Lovely weight. 93/100

La Versa Testarossa Metodo Classico 1990 Oltrepò Pavese, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Surprisingly fresh, and very complex, with a hint of mushroom as well as crystalline citrus fruit. Notes of toast, wax, pith and pear, with some peach. This is in a lovely place with nice depth. Still very fresh with a savoury twist. 93/100

title: Hazendal, a Stellenbosch wine estate transformed
summary: Website: https://www.hazendal.co.za/ Hazendal is a historic wine farm in the Bottelary Hills subregion of Stellenbosch that has been transformed. It
content:
Website: https://www.hazendal.co.za/

Hazendal is a historic wine farm in the Bottelary Hills subregion of Stellenbosch that has been transformed. It began as a wheat and livestock farm in 1699, supplying the Dutch East India Company. Then, in the 1700s Hazendal began with vineyards, primarily planting Muscat and Groendruif (Semillon), two of the key grapes of the time.

Fast forward to 2016, and all the vineyards were ripped out and replanted. The problem was virus, and they weren’t producing well. They planted 12 different varieties in 11.8 hectares, and then more recently planted a 2.7 hectare vineyard as a field blend with 13 white varieties. This is a very interesting approach: the different varieties arrived in bundles of 50 from the nursery, and then a few days before planting they were all shuffled, making this a proper old-school field blend.  

Most importantly, a new winemaking talent arrived in 2024, Kiara Scott Farmer. The 2025 vintage thus signalled the beginning of this new era, and I caught up with her (along with some other wine folk) to taste through this new vintage.

Hazendal is an estate winery, making wines solely from their own vineyards. And the Bottelary Hills is a special place in Stellenbosch, although it hasn’t got the accolades that some of the other subregion get, largely because many of the best grapes end up in wines without Bottelary on the label. There’s an influence from the ocean, some 15 km away, and every afternoon a breeze comes through. Soils are weathered granite, almost beach-sandy in places, with some quartz, and then pockets of schist and sandstone. This helps make wines with tension and salinity. The rolling hills top out at about 290 m on the farm. Neighbours include Dubois, Bellevue, Hartenberg, Avalon and Kaapzicht.

Kiara has a style that I really like. These aren’t wines made in a crowd-pleasing way. ‘It’s important for me to be proud of everything I present,’ she says.

She takes a lot of interest in the vineyard, and has Jaco Engelbrecht as a consultant: he’s one of the best. They are converting to organics. And one of the most important aspects of the work is that at harvest time, Kiara targets specific small parcels, even within the same vineyard, doing multiple picks. ‘I’m not a queen of anything,’ she says, ‘but if I was, I’d be the queen of batch picking.’ She adds that this can drive the vineyard team crazy, when she is very directive about which specific ‘vokkers’ (the vines between one trellising pole and the next) need to be picked on a particular day. ‘I can see peoples’ eyes roll. What is Kiara going to do now? Why can’t we just pick the whole row?’ The grapes are picked into 18 kg lug boxes and then chilled overnight in the cold room before processing the next day.

In the winery, the stage of maturity of each pick determines how it is treated. For the reds, this might include whole bunch, whole berry, destemmed and crushed, and destemmed and crushed with the stems added back in. For the whites, it might determine the choice of fermentation vessel.

Kiara is impressive. Everything is intentional, and thought out. These are my notes on the 2025, an impressive set of wines. Bear in mind that because of the style, some of these will develop nicely over time: we are catching them early in their journey. And this is just vintage one of the new regime. There will be fine-tuning and changes based on learning in subsequent vintages. Hazendal is one to watch.

Hazendal Pinot Noir Rosé 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
Quite full pink in colour. Juicy, supple and fresh with lovely cherry and spice notes. This is really appealing, with brightness and juiciness. 92/100 (UK retail £19.99)

Hazendal Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
Kiara says she is not a fan of Sauvignon Blanc, and does a lot of work with this wine to get rid of green characters, even though she picks early, at what she describes as Cap Classique levels of ripeness. She picks multiple times, from 19-22.5 Balling. The early picks go to concrete because there’s a natural deacidification, and she also does a 22% portion with whole berry ferment on skins. As well as concrete, she uses older 500 litre barrels and some ceramics. Juicy, bright and fresh with a lovely citrus drive, showing nice acidity. Juicy, but still textured, with a touch of mineral. Crystalline and delicious with real tension. 93/100 (UK retail £19.99)

Hazendal White Blend 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
This is 0.2 ha of Marsanne and 0.2 ha of Roussanne, from plots with some iron content in the weathered granite. It is picked four times. Nice ripe aromatics with pear and peach as well as some citrus. Lovely texture here, with crystalline citrus, a touch of green apple and some ripe pear. Real precsion, with purity and focus, and a nice mineral streak. 94/100 (UK retail £42.99)

Hazendal Chenin Blanc 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
This is from a 2 hectare block, and Kiara does 8 different picks. Weathered granite with quartz soils, and the vines are planted treinspoor, with two rows very close to each other, and then a normal row, like train tracks. Fermented and aged in 500 litreFrenach oak, wild ferment, malolactic goes if it goes. Lovely texture here with white peach and pear fruit, showing freshness and good acidity. Lovely focus and tension, but also some freshness. Really expressive and crystalline. 95/100 (UK retail £42.99)

Hazendal Syrah 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
A 1.7 hectare block at 280 m that gets hammered by the wind. 8 picks, four winemaking styles (whole bunch, destemmed whole berries, destemmed and crushed, and destemmed and crushed with stems added back). Raised in 500 litre oak and concrete. Floral and expressive with a bloody, peppery edge. Fresh and expressive with nice texture to the black cherry fruit with a touch of saltiness, as well as some olive tapenade. It’s ripe but fresh and a bit crunchy. 94/100 (UK retail £19.99)

Hazendal Pinotage 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa
‘A fickle variety,’ says Kiara. This ripens fast on sandstone and shale rich blocks, producing small berries. The thing about Pinotage (and this is shared by Cinsault) is that left to its own devices, it ferments very fast and hot. And this is what can cause it to taste bitter and weird. So Kiara slows the ferment down by chilling, and even adds dry ice, keeping temperatures at 26-28 C, when left alone it can easily get to 36. The result is a concentrated, structured wine with lovely purity and finesse, showing vivid berry fruits with nice balance and poise. 94/100 (UK retail £42.99)

Hazendal Carignan 2025 Bottelary Hills, Stellenbosch, South Africa (magnum)
Just four rows. A variety with high natural acidity. 30% whole bunch, raised in one 500 litre barrel. Supple with nice elegance showing sweet red fruits. Expressive with lovely cherry and plum fruit, nice sweetness, and some real elegance on the finish. 94/100

UK agent: https://www.museumwines.co.uk/

title: Highlights: Champagne Taittinger Brut Millésimé 2015 France
summary: This is really impressive. I admit, I wasn’t expecting it to be this good. Champagne Taittinger Brut Millésimé 2015 France12.5%
content:
This is really impressive. I admit, I wasn’t expecting it to be this good.

Champagne Taittinger Brut Millésimé 2015 France
12.5% alcohol. Equal parts Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, 70% Grand Crus, 30% Premier Crus. Five years on lees with a dosage of 9 g/l. This is rich, toasty and intense with pear and peach as well as crystalline citrus fruit. Bold and expansive with mid-palate richness, a touch of sweetness, and real length. I love the toasty, spicy deliciousness to this wine, allied with the ripe fruit. There’s just a twist of reduction, too. An almost complete crowd-pleaser of a Champagne. I’ve gone big on this, but I think it deserves the score. 95/100

title: Galiza: a seminar focusing on the wines of Galicia, Spain
summary: For the 2026 edition of Simplesmente Vinho the guest region was Galiza (Galicia) in Spain, and there were nine visiting
content:
For the 2026 edition of Simplesmente Vinho the guest region was Galiza (Galicia) in Spain, and there were nine visiting producers from here. As well as this, there was a special seminar focusing on the wines of Galiza, hosted by Miguel Anxo Besada (of restaurant A Curva) and Antonio Portela. These were the wines shown. It was a brilliant tasting, showing the potential of this part of Spain, as well as its diversity.

There are five Galician appellations represented here: Ribeiro, Rías Baixas (the most famous), Ribeira Sacra, Valdeorras and Monterrei.

Luis Anzio Rodríguez Viña de Martin 2015 Ribeiro, Spain
Full golden colour. Complex toast, spice and lime on the nose. Lovely density on the palate with crystalline citrus and spice with honey and real depth. Such a beautiful wine. 96/100

Jose Luis Mateo Quinta da Muradella 2021 Monterrei, Spain
Taut, fine and slightly waxy with lovely textured pear fruit. Good acidity and nice complexity here. 94/100

Zarate El Palomar 2021 Rías Baixas, Spain
Subtle toast on the limey nose. Real intensity on the palate with vivid lemony fruit as well as some apricot. Really high acidity. Complex, intense and fine, this is quite beautiful in its lively intensity. Amazing complexity. 95/100

Rafael Palacios Sorte O Soro 2023 Valdeorras, Spain
Godello. Lively and crystalline with focused lemon and pear fruit as well as a crystalline edge. Grapefruit and some fine herbal notes on the finish. So delicately nuanced with beautiful fruit. 95/100

Gerrardò Mendez Do Ferreiro Cepas Velhas 2021 Rías Baixas, Spain (magnum)
Reductive with some minerals and cabbage quality. The palate is lively, fresh, mineral and layered with more of the cabbage qualities coming through. 92/100

Bodegas Albamar 69 Arrobas 2021 Rías Baixas, Spain
Albariño. Real power and intensity here with direct lemony fruit with some apricot richness but it always stays chiselled and fresh. Such purity and intensity here. Linear and really fine. 95/100

Adega Algueira Algueira 2009 Ribeira Sacra, Spain
This is Merenzao. Beginning to brown a bit. Malt spice and earth on the nose as well as stewed strawberries. Soft palate with some sweet strawberry and cherry fruit finishing with some brightness. 90/100

Forjas del Salnés Goliardo Caiño 2011 Rías Baixas, Spain
Caiño Redondo. Some herby notes and vinyl reduction on the nose. The palate is fresh and tart with lively red cherry and raspberry fruit. Taut and focused, this must have been very tight on release. 92/100

Telmo Rodríguez As Caborcas 2019 Valdeorras, Spain
Mencía, Merenzao, Sousón, Brancellao, Godello. This is so intense! Floral red fruits but with lifted acidity and a spicy dimension on the nose. The palate is vivid and has high acidity with juicy redcurrant and sour cherry. Finishes with a meaty spicy character and a dash of Campari. 93/100

Adegas Guímaro Finca Capeliños 2020 Ribeira Sacra, Spain
Mencía. Peppery edge to the sweet floral strawberry and cherry fruit. The palate is textural with a spicy framing to the sweet fruit, as well as a touch of savouriness. 94/100

Envínate Lousas Camiño Novo 2021 Ribeira Sacra, Spain
Mencía and Garnacha Tintorera. Floral but with a grainy, savoury twist showing lovely structure and energy with raspberry, cherry and minerals, supported by good acidity. Real precision here, but also some depth. 95/100

title: The Bothey, an interesting wine project from South Africa
summary: Website: https://www.bothey.co.za/wine/ Katja Leinberger and Marcel Hartman own a luxury accommodation call The Bothey, and they also have a range
content:
Website: https://www.bothey.co.za/wine/

Katja Leinberger and Marcel Hartman own a luxury accommodation call The Bothey, and they also have a range of wines under the same name. But rather than going for rather ordinary private lable wines, they’ve worked with the right people, sourcing amazing grapes from top regions and making some quite special bottles. I tried three of them and was really impressed.

The Bothey ‘Harmony’ Old Bush Vine Chenin Blanc 2025 Coastal Region, South Africa
Bush vines planted in the 1970s and 1980s. Used oak. Textured, fine and delicate with a slight salinity. Such texture here with lovely weight, and real precision. Quite special. 94/100

The Bothey ‘Close Ties’ Chardonnay 2025 Elgin, South Africa
12% alcohol. Raised in a 1000 litre foudre. Taut and linear with crystalline citrus fruit and some pear richness. Very linear with a slight saltiness and a bit of struck match reduction. Such finesse and purity. 94/100

The Bothey Royal Bow Grenache Noir 2024 Piekenierskloof, South Africa
13% alcohol. 60% whole cluster, then aged in concrete and foudre. Fresh, supple, floral and elegant with nice linear cherry and raspberry fruit. This shows amazing purity and elegance, as well as finesse. Nice crunchy structure holds everything together. 95/100

title: Loosen Barry: where the Clare Valley meets the Mosel, a Riesling collaboration
summary: Website: https://www.jimbarry.com/news/loosenbarry-unique-collaboration-meeting-minds-shared-obsession Loosen Barry is a fun (and quite serious) joint Riesling project, and I did a deep dive into
content:
Website: https://www.jimbarry.com/news/loosenbarry-unique-collaboration-meeting-minds-shared-obsession

Loosen Barry is a fun (and quite serious) joint Riesling project, and I did a deep dive into it with Sam Barry (of Jim Barry Wines in Australia’s Clare Valley) and Ernst Loosen (of Dr Loosen in Germany’s Mosel).

Sam Barry describes the collaboration as a ‘wild ride’. It’s based on the Florita vineyard in the Clare Valley. ‘This is a very important vineyard in the history of Australian white wine,’ he says. Leo Buring planted it in 1945 with Palomino and Pedro Ximenez, and over the years the vineyard developed quite a reputation. It was used to make Leo Buring sherry, a fino-style wine made with flor (which Buring established with cultures he’d taken from Jerez), called ‘Florita Fino’. The Flor in the name Florita is a reference to biologically aged sherry! ‘Andrew Caillard thinks this is the first Australian white wine to have a vineyard name on the label,’ says Sam. In 1955 John Vickery joined Buring as winemaker, and then in 1962, after the death of Buring, Lindemans bought the vineyard, keeping Vickery on as winemaker.

Vickery decided that Florita should switch to Riesling, and the new plantings were made in 1962. And Vickery began making Leo Buring Rieslings, both from Florita and other Clare sites, which were to sweep up medals and trophies on the show circuit. This was before Chardonnay came onto the scene.

By the 1980s, sunshine-in-a-bottle Chardonnay came on the scene, and in 1986 the Florita vineyard was put on the market by Lindemans. Leo Buring had seven years inventory of Riesling, which was no longer fashionable, but Jim Barry fancied his chances selling it. The vineyard almost broke them: they were paying 20% interest rates and they couldn’t sell the wine. The other hiccup was that Lindemans sent a legal letter saying that even after the purchase, they owned the Florita trademark. It took a decade for the trademark to lapse, and in 2004 Jim Barry trademarked it themselves.

But now Riesling is cool and this is one of the most famous vineyards. It has a reputation for ageing, and Barry keep back 60% each year as library stock.

Florita is in the Watervale subregion of Clare, and it’s on limestone soils. It’s a 30 hectare vineyard, with 5 hectares of the 1962 plantings remaining. It’s mass selection, ungrafted, and this is the bit used to make the 12 000 or so bottles of Florita Riesling each year. They inoculate using neutral Champagne yeast, ferment cold, leave it on fine lees for a few months and then bottle. It’s the tried and trusted formula.

Jim Barry La Florita 2024 Clare Valley, Australia
The third of three La Niña years (cooler), 2024 was the warmer of the three but still had good soil moisture. Linear and bright with good acidity. Juicy, fine and expressive with a slight saltiness and nice fruit. This is quite lovely. 94/100

Ernst (Ernie) Loosen met Peter Barry (Sam’s father) in 1995. It was the start of a long friendship. In 2010 Tom Barry did a vintage with Ernie in the Mosel. ‘It was a crazy vintage, with crazy acid levels,’ says Ernie. They had to deacidify.

Ernie decided he’s quite like to do an Australian Riesling in his grandfather’s style, which is something he’s been working with for a while. The Loosen style has gone back to the way the wines would have been made in the past: keeping the Riesling on its full lees in large barrels for two-to-eight years, a method used from 1880-1920. Peter Barry agreed, and in 2016 Ernie sent the first 3000 litre barrel over. [It actually turned out to be a 2800 litre barrel, one that Ernie’s winemaker Bernie didn’t want any more.]

The wine was made with a natural ferment and kept in the barrel for two years, in a GG Reserve style, and then it was bottled without filtration.

Ernie explains that this long ageing on lees with a tiny bit of microoxygenation keeps the yeasts alive a bit longer, creating a more reductive environment. This integrates the Riesling acidity into the complexity of the wine. Battonage, in contrast, kills the uyeast and increases oxidation. ‘We want ageability,’ says Ernie, ‘and if you don’t kill the yeast you give the wine enormous ageability.’

‘We’ve never done wild ferment on Riesling,’ says Sam. ‘These flavours are something we hadn’t seen in Clare Valley Riesling.’

On his visit in 2016 Ernie asked whether Florita was the vineyard with the longest hang time. It turned out that another vineyard, Lodge Hill, which is on slate, has more hang time and flavour maturity. So Ernie chose a block here planted in 1980, and told them to hold off picking for a few days to build more flavour, and then press a bit harder. Typically the juice yield from Florita is 500 litres a tonne (this is low, indicating light pressing), whereas for Lodge Hill for Ernie, it’s 560 litres a tonne. Still not high, but more than Florita.

The Lodge Hill is the source for the collaboration wine, Wolta Wolta (this is the traditional name for the Lodge Hill site). In 2023 a second wine was added to the collaboration: Slate Hill. This is wild ferment and then ageing for 2 years on gross lees in stainless steel.

Barry Loosen Slate Hill Riesling 2023 Clare Valley, Australia
Fine, stony and delicate with some apricot and white peach exoticism. Textural and refined with nice stoniness and a crystalline citrus character. Very fine. 94/100

In terms of closures for Wolta Wolta, Ernie wanted to use cork, and sent 4000 bottles and NDTech corks (tested individually for TCA) to Australia. But Barry didn’t have the technology for bottling them, so they used screwcaps. Anyone looking for 4000 Riesling bottles and taint-free corks should make them an offer. [Ernie surveyed his buyers in the USA about their attitude to closures. They came back with a clear message: screwcap for anything under $30, cork for anything more than this.]

A new Jim Barry Riesling wine is in the works: Florita Solera, a blend of Florita across vintages, aged on lees. Wolta Wolta is priced at A$120 and broke the A$60 ceiling for Riesling in Australia; Forita Solera will break it again, it seems.

Loosen Barry Wolta Wolta Riesling 2022 Clare Valley, Australia
This is taut and focused, but has some richness. Lovely citrus drive with crystalline lemon and a touch of pear. Bold, concentrated and textural with nice density and potential for development. Youthful. 94/100

Loosen Barry Wolta Wolta Riesling 2017 Clare Valley, Australia
Such texture here with citrus and pear fruit, as well as hints of apple and aniseed. Broad but fresh with precision, and in a super place now. 95/100

Loosen Barry Wolta Wolta Riesling 2016 Clare Valley, Australia
This is also in a lovely place. There’s a slight creamy element with amazing melon, pear and citrus fruit, opening up beautifully with some richness and texture, and a hint of apricot on the finish. Amazing depth and weight here with real finesse. 96/100

Dr Loosen Erdner Prälat Auslese Goldkapsel 2023 Mosel, Germany
9% alcohol. This is almost 100% botrytis. Linear and mineral with apricot, pear and some melon, as well as great acidity. Youthful, tensile and crystalline. Beautiful. 95/100

title: All Good Things: tasting three examples from this new supermarket-targeted brand
summary: All Good Things This is a new brand focusing on Australia and New Zealand, with appealing, direct packaging. They are
content:
All Good Things

This is a new brand focusing on Australia and New Zealand, with appealing, direct packaging. They are designed for supermarket shelves and there’s some promotional wiggle in the pricing it seems (the list price is somewhat inflated to allow regular discounting to drive sales: they are listed at £9.75-10, but seem to be selling at £8).

All Good Things Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Western Australia
12% alcohol. Zesty citrussy nose is bright and fruity, although there’s not a lot of Sauvignon Blanc character. The palate is light and fruity, with bright lemon and pear fruit, but it’s a bit dilute. Perfectly OK, if you are looking for a generic, crisp dry white wine. 81/100

All Good Things Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Marlborough, New Zealand
12.5% alcohol. There’s some trade-mark elderflower and citrus zest on the nose with a hint of green. The palate is juicy and lively, with nice depth of fruit and good acidity, as well as a touch of sweetness that rounds things out. This tastes of Marlborough Sauvignon. 87/100

All Good Things Shiraz 2024 Western Australia
13.5% alcohol. Spice, chocolate and red berries on the nose, which is sweet and appealing. The palate has rounded berry fruit with a touch of coffee and vanilla adding a nice framing, and a bit of complexity. Some mint/eucalypt character too, with the sweet fruit coming to the fore on the finish. Cleverly put together, this has broad appeal. 86/100

title: Canadian Sparkling Wine: a rare tasting crossing the country, with 24 different wines
summary: Canadian Sparkling Wine is a category that is progressing nicely. This tasting was a selection of 24, across many different
content:
Canadian Sparkling Wine is a category that is progressing nicely. This tasting was a selection of 24, across many different regions. Because of laws restricting inter-provincial shipping of wine, it’s difficult to get a line-up like this. These aren’t all of the best fizzes that Canada makes, but it’s a nice selection showing some of the diversity, with some real highlights. Niagara is slightly over-represented here because this is where the tasting took place.

NIAGARA

Trius Brut NV Niagara, Canada
50% from 2024, and 75% Chardonnay, 25% Pinot Noir. Bright and fresh with nice citrus drive. This has great balance and is fruit driven. Juicy, fresh and very tasty. 90/100

Trius Showcase Blanc de Blancs NV Niagara, Canada
This is a blend of 2011, 2012 and 2013, raised in neutral French oak, then 10 years on lees before being disgorged in September 2024. Lovely focused citrus nose is very pure, with nice toasty detail, and notes of bread and salt. Lively, linear and focused with real complexity and finesse. 93/100

Kew Vineyards Tradition 2021 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
4 g/l dosage. Fruity and bright with nice detail. Has pear and a touch of peach, showing warmth and balance. 89/100

Kew Vineyards Blanc de Blancs 2021 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Lovely bright lemony fruit with some pear and apple. Fruity with nice density, and a touch of richness. 88/100

Kew Vineyards Blanc de Noirs 2020 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Pinot Noir. Cherries and spice with nice density. Rich with some fruit sweetness and some spiciness. 90/100

Kew Vineyards Rosalie 2019 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Skin contact Pinot Noir. Sweet and sour with cherries and spice, as well as a nice citrus drive, and a touch of orange peel. 89/100

Westcott Brilliant 2020 Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
45% Pinot Noir, 45% Chardonnay, 10% Pinot Meunier. Base wine has 10% barrel fermentation, wild ferment for all base wine. Four years on lees then disgorged with 5 g/l dosage. Lovely citrus drive with impact, and a touch of pithiness under the lively lemony fruit. Nice depth and intensity here. 92/100

Westcott Brilliant Blanc de Noirs NV Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
Two-thirds 2020 and one-third perpetual reserve. Barrel fermented in puncheons on the previous year’s lees. Freeze some juice for the liqueur for tirage, no adding yeast at this stage. Creamy and toasty with nice texture and some warmth. Some toast from the barrel ferment and a touch of spice. Broad, satisfying and refined. 93/100

York Brut NV Niagara on the Lake, Canada
This is 2018, the first vintage, although it is labelled NV. Focused, fresh and taut with nice lemony fruit, but also a bit of richness. Powerful with nice density. Stylish. 92/100

York Brut Rosé NV Niagara on the Lake, Canada
2017, first vintage, 100% Pinot Noir, short skin maceration to get colour. Fruity and fine with notes of orange peel, pear and citrus. Has some subtle toast. Textured and quite luxurious. 92/100

York Reserve 2016 Niagara on the Lake, Canada
60% Chardonnay, 40% Pinot Noir, base wine has 2 years in older French oak. Then 6 years on lees. This is complex and layered, toasty and lively. Nice peach, spice, pear and citrus with real complexity and power. 94/100

Malivoire Bisous Brut NV Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
70% Chardonnay, 23% Pinot Noir, 7% Pinot Gris. 2020 base, 3 years on lees, 6 g/l dosage. Fresh, bright and pithy with nice citrus drive. Fruity and expressive. Tart and linear with a juicy finish. 91/100

Malivoire Bisous Blanc de Gamay 2023 Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
One year on lees after base wine aged in used French oak, 6 g/l dosage. Taut, fresh and linear with some bright pithiness and a touch of cherry on the nose. Juicy, herby palate with nice brightness. Has a slight saltiness. 90/100

Malivoire Bisous Rosé NV Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
2023 base year, 2 years on lees, 8 g/l dosage. Very pale with lovely juiciness and tight cherry fruit with a good citrus drive. Juicy and fruity with a slight saltiness and nice purity. 91/100

Malivoire Bisous Noir 2023 West Niagara, Canada
75% Pinot Noir, 25% Gamay, one week on skins, one year on lees. Red in colour, this is fruity and bright with lively cherry and plum fruit. Nice red fruit character. Juicy and refined, lovely stuff. 92/100

QUEBEC

Domaine Saint Jacques Brut 2023 Quebec, Canada
24 months on lees, a blend of Chardonnay and Vidal. Fruity and bright with nice lemon and pear fruit. Juicy and linear with good acidity and admirable purity of fruit. Refined. 91/100

Domaine Bergeville Le Blanc 2024 Quebec, Canada
Some unusual notes on the nose: I thought it might be corked, but it wasn’t. Herbal, lemony and bright with pear and peach fruit as well as some pithiness. Juicy with some complexity, and quite distinctive. 88/100

NOVA SCOTIA

Benjamin Bridge Methode Classique NV Nova Scotia, Canada
11% alcohol. A blend of grapes including some hybrid in this cuvée. Fresh and linear with nice pithy hints. Tart and lively with a lovely lemony drive, some tightness and a slight herby character. Saline twist on the finish. Very fine. 93/100

Avondale Sky Blanc de Noir 2017 Nova Scotia, Canada
Fresh, fruity and lively with nice herb and toast complexity. Rich and layered with lots of flavour. 90/100

L’Acadie Prestige Brut 2019 Nova Scotia, Canada
Juicy, bright and fresh with nice pithiness. Some grapey richness as well as focused lemony fruit. Bright and linear with nice precision. 90/100

VANCOUVER ISLAND

Blue Grouse Sparkling Cuvée 2020 Cowichan Valley, Vancouver Island, Canada
Fruity, bright and linear with nice lemon and herb notes. Tart and lively with nice precision. 89/100

OKANAGAN/SIMILKAMEEN/FRASER VALLEY

Corcelettes MT 2022 Similkameen, BC, Canada
Juicy, bright and lemony with tartness and good acidity. Nice fruitiness here with a  good acid line. 88/100

Terravista Vineyards En Terre 2022 Okanagan, BC, Canada
Juicy and bright with nice cherry and citrus fruit, with a compact character. Lively, bright and stylish. 91/100

Township 7 Sirius 2017 Fraser Valley, BC, Canada
Focused and quite toasty, showing nice complexity. There’s a saline edge to the focused citrus fruit, as well as some spicy complexity. Stylish 93/100
